Robert Ben Garant’s Weekly World News Comedy Takes Aim at Tabloid Absurdity

Robert Ben Garant and Cathy Shim are developing an improvised comedy around Weekly World News, the tabloid known for outrageous stories and Bat Boy.

By LokkeeVerse · 3 min read

Weekly World News, the tabloid synonymous with outrageous supernatural scoops and the enduring figure of Bat Boy, is headed toward a television comedy adaptation. According to Vulture, citing Deadline, Robert Ben Garant is developing an improvised series centered on the publication, with Garant and Cathy Shim serving as showrunners. The pairing brings a familiar name in ensemble comedy to a brand whose fantastical headlines already operate close to parody.

A Tabloid Built for Comic Possibilities

Weekly World News established its identity through sensational accounts of aliens, strange creatures and impossible discoveries, presented with the confidence of newspaper reporting. Its appeal rests on that contrast: extraordinary claims delivered in an ordinary journalistic package. Bat Boy, its signature half-human, half-bat character, became an especially recognizable expression of that approach.

That sensibility offers fertile ground for a television comedy. A publication devoted to the unbelievable can support stories about both bizarre subjects and the people trying to turn them into headlines. The central creative question is how the adaptation will use that world: as a workplace setting, a springboard for fantastical encounters, or some combination of the two. Those possibilities are not confirmed plot details.

Why Improvisation Fits the Premise

Garant’s background includes the sketch-comedy troupe The State and the improvisational television comedy Reno 911!, making the announced format a notable part of the project. Improvised comedy can draw energy from performers reacting to one another within a planned situation, rather than relying exclusively on fixed dialogue. An outlandish tabloid premise gives that approach plenty of room for escalation.

The challenge will be finding a consistent comic perspective beyond the novelty of individual headlines. Weekly World News’s exaggerated style emerged from a print-tabloid culture; television must also sustain characters, relationships and stories. In a media environment where fabricated claims can spread without their original context, the distinction between affectionate fantasy and satire of misinformation could also shape how audiences read the show.

  • **The project:** An improvised comedy centered on Weekly World News.
  • **The creative leads:** Robert Ben Garant and Cathy Shim are reported as showrunners.
  • **The attraction:** A recognizable tabloid identity with a long tradition of fantastical storytelling.
  • **The open question:** How that identity will translate into an ongoing television format.

Readers should watch for announcements about a network or streaming home, casting, production plans and the show’s eventual structure. Those developments will clarify how far the project has progressed—and whether its best-known tabloid creations become central characters or remain part of the surrounding comic universe.
